extracted.intended_audience: Authors, editors, and reviewers of systematic reviews and meta-analyses in health care (researchers preparing or evaluating SRs/MAs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to transparently and completely report systematic reviews (with or without meta-analysis) of health care interventions, using a 27-item checklist and a four-phase flow diagram (the PRISMA Statement). Intended to help authors present what was planned, done, and found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the report as a systematic review, meta-analysis, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explicitly use the terms 'systematic review' and/or 'meta-analysis' in the title to improve indexing and identification. Prefer informative titles that reflect interventions, comparators, outcomes, and study design (PICOS). Avoid vague terms like 'review' or oversimplifying declarative titles that state conclusions; indicative titles that describe scope are generally preferred. Examples provided demonstrate inclusion of design and topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured summary (Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a structured summary including, as applicable: background; objectives; data sources; study eligibility criteria, participants, and interventions; study appraisal and synthesis methods; results; limitations; conclusions and implications of key findings; funding for the systematic review; and systematic review registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a structured abstract with headings (e.g., Context/Background; Objective; Data Sources; Study Selection; Study Appraisal and Synthesis Methods; Results; Limitations; Conclusions/Implications). Report main numerical results (number of trials/participants, pooled estimates and CIs), key limitations, funding, and registration number if available. Balance completeness with journal space limits; structured abstracts facilitate clarity and retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale (Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of what is already known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the review is important from perspectives like public health, patient care, or policy. State whether the report is new or an update, and, if an update, explain what has changed. Provide brief summary of current knowledge and gaps, and indicate what the review aims to add.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an explicit statement of questions being addressed with reference to participants, interventions, comparisons, outcomes, and study design (PICOS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State precise review questions using PICOS elements (population, intervention/exposure, comparator, outcomes, study design). Clearly framed objectives define eligibility criteria and search strategy. Objectives may be narrow or broad depending on aims; be explicit so readers can judge scope and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol and registration (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if a review protocol exists, if and where it can be accessed (e.g., Web address), and, if available, provide registration information including registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report existence and location of an a priori protocol. Describe any protocol amendments and their rationale. Protocols help limit biased post hoc decisions (e.g., selective outcome reporting). Registration (when available) increases transparency and may reduce duplication of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify study characteristics (e.g., PICOS, length of follow-up) and report characteristics (e.g., years considered, language, publication status) used as criteria for eligibility, giving rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly specify types of studies, participants, interventions/comparators, outcomes, study designs, timeframes, languages, and publication status included or excluded, and explain reasons. Give sufficient detail so readers understand the scope and can judge potential sources of heterogeneity or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sources (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all information sources (e.g., databases with dates of coverage, contact with study authors to identify additional studies) in the search and date last searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List databases searched with coverage dates, handsearching, conference abstracts, trial registries, contact with investigators, and other sources. Provide the date of the last search. Transparently reporting sources aids reproducibility and assessment of completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search (Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present full electronic search strategy for at least one database, including any limits used, such that it could be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the complete search string (keywords, MeSH terms), any filters or limits (dates, languages), and justification for limits. Providing at least one full search strategy enables reproducibility and allows readers to judge comprehensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study selection (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the process for selecting studies (i.e., screening, eligibility, included in systematic review, and, if applicable, included in the meta-analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how records were screened and selected (e.g., number of reviewers, independent screening, resolution of disagreements). Provide or refer to a flow diagram showing numbers at each stage (identification, screening, eligibility, inclusion) and reasons for exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection process (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe method of data extraction from reports (e.g., piloted forms, independently, in duplicate) and any processes for obtaining and confirming data from investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether data extraction was done using piloted forms, by how many reviewers, whether independently and in duplicate, and procedures to contact authors for missing or unclear data. Describe methods to verify extracted data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data items (Item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: List and define all variables for which data were sought (e.g., PICOS, funding sources) and any assumptions and simplifications made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a list of all extracted variables, definitions, units, timepoints, and any assumptions used (e.g., imputations). Reporting funding sources of primary studies is encouraged because it may be relevant to bias assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias in individual studies (Item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods used for assessing risk of bias of individual studies (including specification of whether this was done at the study or outcome level), and how this information is to be used in any data synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the tool or criteria used (e.g., Cochrane risk-of-bias domains), whether assessment was per study or per outcome, who assessed risk of bias and how disagreements were resolved, and whether risk-of-bias judgments informed inclusion, sensitivity analyses, or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary measures (Item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the principal summary measures (e.g., risk ratio, difference in means).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare primary effect measures and metrics (e.g., RR, OR, mean difference, standardized mean difference). Explain any conversions, scales, and rationale for chosen measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis of results (Item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the methods of handling data and combining results of studies, if done, including measures of consistency (e.g., I2) for each meta-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify models used (fixed vs random effects), methods for pooling, handling of multi-arm trials, treatment of missing data, and statistical measures for heterogeneity (I2, Q). Explain choices and thresholds used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias across studies (Item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify any assessment of risk of bias that may affect the cumulative evidence (e.g., publication bias, selective reporting within studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe methods to assess across-study biases (e.g., funnel plots, formal tests for small-study effects, searching for unpublished studies), and how the results affect confidence in cumulative estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional analyses (Item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods of additional analyses (e.g., sensitivity or subgroup analyses, meta-regression), if done, indicating which were pre-specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State pre-specified vs exploratory analyses, rationale for subgroup/sensitivity analyses or meta-regression, methods used, and how findings were interpreted relative to primary analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study selection — Results (Item 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give numbers of studies screened, assessed for eligibility, and included in the review, with reasons for exclusions at each stage, ideally with a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts at each stage of the review process and reasons for exclusion. Present the four-phase flow diagram (identification, screening, eligibility, included) to summarise study selection transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study characteristics (Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each study, present characteristics for which data were extracted (e.g., study size, PICOS, follow-up period) and provide the citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulate or describe study design, participants, interventions, comparators, outcomes, follow-up, settings, and key baseline characteristics, with citations to the original reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias within studies — Results (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present data on risk of bias of each study and, if available, any outcome-level assessment (see Item 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results of risk-of-bias assessments (per study and/or per outcome), ideally in tables or figures, and link these assessments to study findings when interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of individual studies (Item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: For all outcomes considered (benefits or harms), present, for each study: (a) simple summary data for each intervention group and (b) effect estimates and confidence intervals, ideally with a forest plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide raw or summary data per study and the effect estimates with confidence intervals. Use forest plots where appropriate to visually display study-level and pooled estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis of results — Results (Item 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results of each meta-analysis done, including confidence intervals and measures of consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report pooled estimates, CIs, heterogeneity statistics (I2, tau-squared), and interpret clinical and statistical heterogeneity; present subgroup and sensitivity analysis results as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias across studies — Results (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results of any assessment of risk of bias across studies (see Item 15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report findings from funnel plots, tests for small-study effects, and other assessments of reporting bias; discuss potential impact on review conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional analysis — Results (Item 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give results of additional analyses, if done (e.g., sensitivity or subgroup analyses, meta-regression [see Item 16]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report outcomes of pre-specified and exploratory additional analyses, clarifying which were pre-specified, and discuss their implications and limitations (risk of spurious findings, multiple comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of evidence (Item 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the main findings including the strength of evidence for each main outcome; consider their relevance to key groups (e.g., health care providers, users, and policy makers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a balanced summary that addresses certainty/strength of evidence, clinical importance, and applicability to stakeholders; link conclusions closely to the primary objectives and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations (Item 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations at study and outcome level (e.g., risk of bias), and at review level (e.g., incomplete retrieval of identified research, reporting bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly acknowledge limitations of included studies, outcome data, and the review process (search limitations, language/publication restrictions, potential selective reporting), and discuss how these affect confidence in findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions (Item 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a general interpretation of the results in the context of other evidence, and implications for future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret findings considering other available evidence and limitations; suggest implications for practice and prioritize areas for further research, avoiding overstated conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding (Item 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe sources of funding for the systematic review and other support (e.g., supply of data); role of funders for the systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report funding sources and any sponsor roles (design, conduct, analysis, reporting). Disclose potential conflicts of interest and consider how funding might influence review conduct or interpretation.
